public_rationale: Marcus said that failing to follow chess rules was a continuing failure of LLMs. The Register covered a 2024 benchmark of 1,000 chess puzzles. It reported that even GPT-4o, the best model tested, made illegal moves 12.7% of the time, and that most other LLMs made more illegal moves than legal ones. The benchmark's author counts these illegal moves as a failure to internalize the board and the rules. So before the post, leading LLMs did still break chess rules at a meaningful rate. Calling this a failure of 'formal reasoning' is Marcus's interpretation and is not graded.
limitations: The evidence is one puzzle benchmark with a single prompt format. Other formats or full games may give different illegal-move rates.
The benchmark repository's current table is from 2025, so the 2024 figures come from the news report.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs still fail to follow the rules of chess, which is an ongoing failure of formal reasoning.

from_speaker: Failure to follow the rules of chess
our_interpretation: Plain reading: when the post was published, leading LLMs still often made illegal chess moves when asked to play or solve chess positions.
He names no period, so the target period is 2024 up to the post date (2024-10-11). That is the latest state public evidence could describe before the post.
The 'formal reasoning' label is his interpretation of the failure. Only the factual part, that LLMs make illegal moves, is graded here.
criteria.support_condition: A documented evaluation from 2024, before the post, shows that current leading LLMs (including the strongest available ones) make illegal chess moves at a non-trivial rate.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evaluations from the same period show that leading LLMs reliably made only legal moves, so illegal moves were rare or absent.
